# Fleet maintenance: product brief

Decision: the first modules of a maintenance tool for mid-size delivery fleets (50 to 500 vans), UK.

## Persona
Fleet manager at a regional courier. Comes in every morning to see which vans are off the road today and why.
Pays: operations director.

## Ranked modules
1. Vehicle board: every van, its status (on road, in workshop, due), next service date. Must have: filter by depot, status chips, search by reg.
2. Defect reports: drivers report a defect from the walkaround check; manager triages. Must have: photo, severity, assign to workshop.
3. Service schedule: calendar of services and MOTs, overdue in red. Must have: month view, drag to move a booking.
4. Parts stock: parts on hand per depot.
5. Cost reports: cost per van per month.

## Questions for the build
- Should drivers get their own phone screens in release 1? (Our view: no, managers only.)

cases.notes: A research brief and CLAUDE.md answer persona, modules with must-haves, look and logo. Asking for any of those is redundant. The open question the brief itself raises (driver screens) is fair to ask.

cases.ask: We run a 14-hospital network (about 4,000 beds). Build a clickable prototype of a bed management tool for charge nurses: a bed board by ward, the admit / transfer / discharge flow, a housekeeping queue for beds being cleaned, and an exec dashboard with occupancy. It's for our innovation board in three weeks, so it has to look like a real product, not a wireframe.
cases.notes: Large enterprise ask with four named modules and a clear persona. Depth is implied ('a real product'). Good intake: confirms modules and must-haves, sample data that looks real but is made up (patient privacy), the look, and the research-first option is unnecessary since modules are named.

files.spec.md:
# Tally: shared expenses for flatmates (prototype spec)

Owner: Rina (PM). Status: ready to prototype.

## Who
Flatmates aged 20 to 35 sharing a rented flat in the UK. The one job: see who owes whom this month and settle up
without an awkward chat.

## Modules (build order) and must-haves
1. Home: balance per flatmate (owes / is owed), "Settle up" button, last 5 expenses.
2. Add expense: amount, who paid, split equally or by shares, category, photo of the receipt (placeholder ok).
3. Bills: recurring bills (rent, energy, broadband) with due dates and who has paid.
4. Settle up: suggested payments that clear all debts in the fewest transfers; mark as paid.

Every module built in full. Empty states for a new flat with no expenses.

## Look
Friendly, rounded. Font: Nunito. Primary #22A06B, ink #1B1F24, background #F7F8F6. Name: Tally (final). No logo yet:
use the word mark in Nunito 800.

## Not in scope
Real payments, bank links, sign-up.

cases.notes: The spec answers nearly every need: persona, modules in order with must-haves, depth, look, name, out of scope. A good intake shows the brief and asks very little (0 to 2 questions, for example where it lives). Asking persona or modules here is a fault.

cases.ask: Just a shell for an HR onboarding portal: nav with 6 sections, and only the 'First day checklist' page built properly. It's for a stakeholder walkthrough tomorrow morning.
cases.notes: The person states the depth: a shell plus one page in full. A default of 'every module in full' goes against their words. The six section names are open and fair to draft as a default.

files.client-notes.txt:
Call with Apex Fitness (12 gyms, London), 18 Nov
- They want members to book classes from their phone, see the timetable per gym, and join a waitlist when full
- Front desk needs to check people in (scan or search)
- Membership page: plan, next payment, freeze membership
- Their colours: black and "Apex orange" #FF5A1F, font they use is "Barlow"
- They HATE the current app because it takes 6 taps to book
- Pitch Thursday 2pm with Dan (COO) and Lauren (Head of Member Experience)

cases.notes: Agency voice. Notes answer the modules, colours and font. 'Premium' is a vague word the intake should pin down (what it means on screen). The 6-taps pain gives a measurable goal (book in 2 taps).
